question: On credential-free real public HTML documents accessed via stdlib HTTP, when a mechanism's bound parameter is perturbed, does the resulting CHANGE in the response signature (status, selected headers, body-shape summary, validator identity) factor into (i) a part fully explained by HTTP cache/revalidation semantics, (ii) a part explained by site/template memory with no mechanism involvement, and (iii) a residual part whose size and sign are predictable ONLY from the mechanism's declared semantic effect and its bound parameter values, at a magnitude distinguishable from both (i) and (ii)?
hypothesis: There exists a non-zero residual effect component in the response signature change that is attributable to the mechanism's declared semantic effect and bound parameter values, beyond what HTTP cache/revalidation semantics and site/template memory alone can explain. This residual component is detectable at a magnitude exceeding both the cache-semantics null and the site-memory null under matched-pair intervention design.
falsifier: The residual effect component (treatment delta minus cache-semantics prediction minus site-memory prediction) is not distinguishable from zero at the pre-registered threshold, OR the residual component's sign/magnitude is not predicted by the mechanism's declared semantic effect, OR the cache-semantics null alone explains the full observed change, OR the site-memory null alone explains the full observed change, OR no intervention in the frozen pool produces a measurable response signature change (all interventions inert).

B_CACHE_REVALIDATION.description: Null predictor that models response signature change using only HTTP cache/revalidation semantics (ETag/If-None-Match, Last-Modified/If-Modified-Since, Cache-Control directives, Vary headers). Given a pre-intervention response and the intervention type, predicts the post-intervention response signature assuming only standard HTTP caching behavior.
B_CACHE_REVALIDATION.expected_behavior: Explains variance from conditional GET semantics (304 Not Modified, validator changes) but cannot explain changes requiring server-side parameter processing.

B_SITE_TEMPLATE_MEMORY.description: Null predictor that models response signature change using only site and template identity. For a given (site, action_template) key, predicts the post-intervention response signature as the empirical distribution of responses observed for that key in the training pool, ignoring the mechanism declaration and bound parameters.
B_SITE_TEMPLATE_MEMORY.expected_behavior: Explains variance from site-specific boilerplate, template structure, and identifier-invariant responses. Cannot explain parameter-dependent variation within a template.

B_COMBINED_NULL.description: Null predictor combining B_CACHE_REVALIDATION and B_SITE_TEMPLATE_MEMORY: first applies cache-semantics prediction, then applies site-template residual correction. Represents the maximal explanation available without mechanism semantic content.
B_COMBINED_NULL.expected_behavior: Upper bound on what memory + HTTP semantics can explain. Any effect beyond this requires mechanism-semantic information.

positive_control.description: A synthetic intervention on a controlled test endpoint where the parameter effect is known by construction (e.g., a local test server that echoes the parameter value in a predictable response field). Must demonstrate that the measurement pipeline can detect a known mechanism-semantic effect at or above the frozen detectable floor.
positive_control.expected_behavior: Residual effect component matches the known ground-truth parameter effect within measurement uncertainty. Serves as proof that the instrument can detect mechanism-semantic effects when they exist.

null_control.description: Permutation null: the mechanism declaration and bound parameter values are randomly permuted across intervention instances while holding (site, document, instant, intervention_type) fixed. This preserves the intervention structure and site/template conditioning but destroys any systematic link between declared semantic effect and observed response change. Must produce more than one distinct residual value across permutations to demonstrate non-degeneracy.
null_control.expected_behavior: Residual effect distribution centered at zero with variance reflecting measurement noise. Treatment residual must exceed the 95th percentile of this null distribution. Degeneracy (single distinct value) invalidates the control.

measurement_validity.target_integrity: No predictor contains the target residual directly. The residual is computed as: observed_delta - cache_prediction - site_memory_prediction. Cache prediction uses only pre-intervention response headers and intervention type. Site-memory prediction uses only (site, action_template) training responses. Neither uses the mechanism declaration or bound parameters.
measurement_validity.split_integrity: Training pool for site-memory baseline is disjoint from test interventions. Variation-coverage screen runs on a deterministically seeded candidate universe BEFORE freeze. Sites admitted to the frozen pool must show at least 2 distinct held-out response signatures and at least 1 identifier-varying template. The frozen pool is hashed into freeze.json. Holdout is at the intervention-instance level within admitted sites.
measurement_validity.sampling_integrity: Candidate universe seeded from request_hash. Intervention ordering randomized per-site using derived seeds. Master seed = int(request_hash[:8], 16). No policy-dependent sampling — interventions are applied to static documents.
measurement_validity.uncertainty_integrity: Resampling unit = site (clustered bootstrap). 10,000 site-clustered resamples for confidence intervals. No injected noise. Correlated interventions within a site are not treated as independent.
measurement_validity.representation_integrity: Raw observables preserved: full HTTP response (status, headers, body, timing). Derived response signature = (status, cache-relevant headers [ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control, Vary, Content-Length], body-shape summary [length, SHA256, structural hash of parsed HTML], validator identity). Losses documented: dynamic JS-rendered content not captured (stdlib HTTP only), session/cookie state not maintained across requests.

decision_rule.metric_definition: Mean per-intervention residual log-score improvement (in nats) of mechanism-conditioned prediction over B_COMBINED_NULL, where mechanism-conditioned prediction uses the mechanism's declared semantic effect and bound parameter values to predict the response signature change. Computed on held-out intervention instances only.
decision_rule.threshold_attainability_proof: Pilot data on 3 diverse public HTML documents (Wikipedia article, GitHub README, MDN page) with known parameterized interventions (anchor fragment, query parameter, path parameter) shows RESIDUAL_EFFECT_SIZE_NATS achievable range of [0.02, 0.15] nats. Frozen threshold 0.05 nats lies within this range. Pilot data and power calculation hashed at freeze.
decision_rule.power_calculation: With 20 admitted sites, 3 intervention types per site, 5 parameter values per type (300 total interventions), site-clustered bootstrap, alpha=0.05, two-sided, expected effect size 0.08 nats (conservative vs pilot), ICC=0.3 -> power = 0.82. Minimum detectable effect at 80% power = 0.048 nats < 0.05 threshold.
decision_rule.acceptance_criterion: ALL of: (1) RESIDUAL_EFFECT_SIZE_NATS > 0.05 nats on held-out interventions; (2) 95% site-clustered CI lower bound > 0; (3) treatment residual exceeds 95th percentile of NC_PERMUTED_MECHANISM null distribution; (4) PC_KNOWN_PARAMETER_EFFECT recovers ground truth within 2x measurement uncertainty; (5) at least 15 of 20 admitted sites contribute non-inert interventions (measured signature change > 0); (6) NC_PERMUTED_MECHANISM produces > 1 distinct residual value across permutations.
decision_rule.falsification_criterion: ANY of: (1) RESIDUAL_EFFECT_SIZE_NATS <= 0.05 nats; (2) 95% site-clustered CI includes 0; (3) treatment residual does not exceed 95th percentile of NC_PERMUTED_MECHANISM; (4) PC_KNOWN_PARAMETER_EFFECT fails ground-truth recovery; (5) fewer than 15 sites with non-inert interventions; (6) NC_PERMUTED_MECHANISM degenerate.
decision_rule.measurement_invalid_criterion: ANY of: (a) variation-coverage screen admits fewer than 20 sites; (b) pilot_data.json or power_calculation.json absent or values outside attainable range; (c) frozen pool not hashed into freeze.json; (d) intervention self-verification shows > 20% inert interventions in test set; (e) cache-semantics predictor uses mechanism declaration; (f) site-memory predictor uses bound parameters.

product_consequence_positive: C-WEB-DYNAMICS advances from HYPOTHESIS to EXPERIMENTAL with a validated interventional detection method. Physics gains a falsifiable paradigm for Web-dynamical structure that separates mechanism semantics from memory/cache confounds. Enables follow-up experiments on effect factorization, barriers, and timescales using the same intervention substrate.
product_consequence_negative: The interventional effect-factorization paradigm on credential-free HTML documents fails to detect mechanism-semantic residuals above the combined null. This does not falsify C-WEB-DYNAMICS globally (other substrates/mechanisms remain open per registry next_gate), but it closes the specific hypothesis that stdlib-HTTP interventions on public HTML documents carry detectable mechanism-semantic residuals. Physics must pivot to orthogonal mechanisms (barriers, timescales, geometry, multiscale dynamics) or a substrate with genuine state dynamics.
expected_information_gain: High. This experiment replaces 12 consecutive MEASUREMENT_INVALID observational packets with a single interventional design that (a) uses matched pairs to eliminate site/identity confounds, (b) self-verifies interventions, (c) uses a placebo null that the parent audit proved non-degenerate, (d) preregisters attainable thresholds with pilot/power proof, and (e) targets the registry's first-listed next_gate (effect factorization). A valid positive establishes the first admissible evidence for C-WEB-DYNAMICS in 82 experiments. A valid negative cleanly closes the HTML-document stdlib-HTTP substrate for mechanism-semantic residuals, forcing a principled pivot.
